confirmed_root_causes: Primary root cause is confirmed: Build Arena requires the live LLM to manually emit a gate-perfect contract graph (every directed cross-component import edge, in the correct direction), but those contracts are mechanically derivable from the import graph plus component ownership. The gate's own helpers (_component_pairs_for_import_edge, _edge_supports_contract, _check_owned_import_edge_coverage) already compute the required pairs, so demanding the model reproduce them is redundant deterministic bookkeeping pushed onto a probabilistic generator.

The evidence cleanly supports this: across both attempts edge_coverage stayed flat at 13 while contract_references (5->1) and component_measurability (6->2) fell under a better prompt. An invariant-to-prompting failure class is the signature of mechanical bookkeeping, not semantic interpretation. The gate is therefore correct to block, and the seam to fix is ingestion-side contract closure, not the gate.

Secondary root cause is confirmed and directly reproduced by code inspection: DiffProposerRunner.apply() rejects a non-existent target before transport (the explicit exists()/is_file() guard), while project_intake_scorecard + proposer_handoff can legitimately select an absence finding (docs/index.md). Capability mismatch, not a transport or auth issue.

The non-root-cause eliminations (xAI auth/model availability, target staleness, local fmc-mcp test/lint/typecheck health, secret leakage / sk- false positive) are each backed by concrete evidence and are correctly excluded.
corrections: Reframe 'derive all mechanically knowable cross-component import contracts from the graph and component ownership' precisely: contract DIRECTION is mechanical (import edges are directed), but contract EXISTENCE/correctness is only as trustworthy as the component-ownership assignment, which is at least partly LLM-supplied (that is what component_measurability is policing). Closure is deterministic given ownership; it does not make ownership itself trustworthy. State this explicitly so the fix is not oversold as making the result fully deterministic.

After closure, the gate's edge_coverage check becomes a check on Build Arena's own generated output rather than an independent check on the model. That is acceptable IF and ONLY IF edge_coverage was always purely mechanical. Document this so a future reader does not assume edge_coverage still constrains the LLM. The remaining real LLM-constraining signal lives in component_measurability/responsibilities and any non-import (semantic/data/runtime) contracts.

Confirm whether the 2 residual component_measurability failures in attempt 2 are caused by absent contracts (closure will fix) or by absent/weak responsibility text (closure will NOT fix). The note assumes closure resolves measurability via contract attachment; that holds only for the contract-dependent sub-check, not for responsibility-text sub-checks.
implementation_warnings: Ordering hazard in the proposer: protected-path, read-only-path, and multi-target rejection MUST run before the relaxed existence check, or new-file support becomes a hole that lets writes into protected paths that happen not to exist yet.

Closure must be idempotent and deterministic across runs (stable contract IDs and ordering keyed on edge IDs), or the final identity/hash of the Project Model will be unstable and break freshness/reproducibility guarantees.

Watch for double-counting / conflicts when the model DID emit a correct contract for an edge: closure must normalize (dedupe, fix direction) rather than append a second contract.auto.* alongside the model's, which could trip contract_references or measurability in a new way.

git apply --check for a new file requires a well-formed diff (/dev/null -> b/path, 'new file mode 100644', correct hunk header). A model returning an a/path with content for a non-existent file will fail; the prompt/transport must instruct empty source explicitly and validate_unified_diff must accept the new-file shape.

Path normalization on a non-existent target: realpath/abspath behavior differs for missing files; ensure boundary containment is computed against the resolved parent directory, not the (unresolvable) missing leaf, to avoid both false rejects and escapes.

Add the tests BEFORE the closure/proposer changes (the note's step 3) and include a negative test proving an unowned-endpoint or reversed-but-unownable edge still fails the gate, so closure cannot be shown to have silently weakened coverage.
missing_evidence: The actual textual content of a representative sample of the 13 edge_coverage and the contract_references violations is not quoted, only the counts and classes. Quote 2-3 raw violations to prove every one reduces to (edge_id, required_from_component, required_to_component) closure rather than a contract the model must still author semantically.

No confirmation that the gate requires ONLY import-edge-derived contracts. If the gate (or component_measurability) also requires non-import contracts (data/runtime/API contracts) that are not mechanically derivable from import edges, closure will not fully unblock and the LLM must still supply those.

No confirmation of the provenance/trustworthiness of the component-ownership mapping that closure will consume. If ownership is LLM-emitted, show that a wrong ownership assignment is independently caught (e.g., by measurability) before closure runs, otherwise closure can manufacture a gate-passing-but-wrong Project Model.

For the proposer fix, no evidence yet that validate_unified_diff and the boundary/path-normalization logic behave correctly for a path that does not exist on disk (realpath/symlink resolution on missing files, /dev/null source + 'new file mode' header handling).
simplicity_guidance: Keep contract closure as a single pure transform between ingestion and gate: input (raw model output + import graph + ownership) -> output (model with auto-contracts added). No new gate flags, no gate relaxation, no special-casing inside the gate. The gate stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

Mark generated contracts distinctly (contract.auto.<edge-id>) and never mutate the on-disk raw model artifact; closure operates on the in-memory/derived model used for the gate so the audit trail stays intact. This is already in the note — hold the line on it.

Do not let closure invent components, rename components, or reassign ownership. It only adds/normalizes contracts for edges whose BOTH endpoints already map to existing components. If an edge's endpoints are unowned, leave the failure to the gate — that is genuine semantic signal.

For the proposer, scope the change to the narrowest case: single target, missing file, in-scope + boundary-safe, empty file_contents, exactly-one-new-file diff. Do not generalize to multi-file or directory creation in this slice.

Reuse existing primitives (validate_unified_diff, git apply --check, existing boundary/protected-path checks) rather than adding a parallel new-file code path. The only delta should be relaxing the pre-transport existence guard under guarded conditions.
